name: Nvidia
what: Designs the chips and software most AI models are trained and run on.

current.label: Latest quarter revenue (Aug–Oct 2026)
current.detail: Data center revenue $107.6B, up 110%. Gross margin 74.8%. Net income $65.3B.

future.label: Company outlook, next quarter
future.detail: Plus or minus 3%, in a quarter with one extra week. Gross margin guided to 71%–72%. Assumes no data-center compute sales to China.

drivers: Cloud giants and AI labs racing to build data centers
Each new chip generation sells at higher prices
CUDA software keeps developers on Nvidia hardware
risks: A few huge customers buy most of its chips
Export limits to China and new license rules for Southeast Asia
Leadership change: founder resigned, interim CEO while the board searches
Receivables and inventory roughly doubled since January
Any slowdown in AI spending would hit fast
watch: Data center growth each quarter
Gross margin recovering from the 71%–72% guide
Receivables and inventory versus sales
Who the board names as permanent CEO
why: Every major tech company is racing to build AI data centers, and most AI models are trained and run on Nvidia chips. Sales more than doubled from a year earlier to $115.8 billion last quarter, and it kept about 75 cents of each revenue dollar as gross profit. Its CUDA software makes switching to another chipmaker slow and costly, and its interim CEO says demand still exceeds supply.

company: Next quarter revenue of about $130B, plus or minus 3%, including an extra week (guidance, Nov 17, 2026)
Gross margin of 71%–72% next quarter as new Vera Rubin systems ramp; interim CEO Colette Kress pointed to margin improvement in fiscal 2028
Purchase commitments rose to $390B in the quarter, per the earnings call (Kiplinger)
analysts: Before the report, analysts expected about $108.8B of revenue and $2.47 of adjusted EPS; Nvidia reported $115.8B and $2.68 (Kiplinger, Nov 17, 2026)
Analysts are watching whether the company can execute without its founder; the board says it does not intend to bring Jensen Huang back

scenarios.bull: Vera Rubin ramps smoothly, margins recover as promised, receivables are collected on schedule, and a strong permanent CEO is named.
scenarios.base: Growth slows from triple digits as comparisons get tougher, but stays strong while data-center building continues and supply remains tight.
scenarios.bear: Big customers pay more slowly or cut orders, inventory has to be written down, margins stay lower, and the leadership search drags on.

name: Micron Technology
what: Makes memory chips (DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory) that every AI server needs.

past.label: Fiscal 2026 revenue (year to Aug 2026)
past.detail: Up from $37.4B in fiscal 2025, about 3.6 times larger.

current.label: Latest quarter revenue (Jun–Aug 2026)
current.detail: Versus $11.3B a year earlier. Gross margin 86.8%.

drivers: AI servers need far more high-bandwidth memory
Tight memory supply lets prices rise
Only three big memory makers worldwide
risks: Memory is famously cyclical: booms are followed by price crashes
Samsung and SK hynix are adding capacity
Margins this high rarely last
watch: Memory prices
Competitors' new factory capacity
Gross margin direction
why: AI servers need huge amounts of high-bandwidth memory, and only three companies make it at scale: Micron, Samsung and SK hynix. Supply is tight, so memory prices have soared. That pushed Micron's gross margin to 86.8% last quarter, extraordinary for a memory company.

company: Next quarter revenue of about $61.5B, plus or minus $1.5B, up from $54.2B
analysts: Analysts debate how long the memory upcycle lasts: past booms ended when new factories came online and prices fell

scenarios.bull: AI demand keeps memory scarce into 2027 and beyond, and margins stay near record highs.
scenarios.base: Growth continues but slows as competitors' new capacity arrives and prices level off.
scenarios.bear: Supply catches up, memory prices fall fast, and profits drop sharply, as in past memory busts.

name: Microsoft
what: Sells cloud computing (Azure), Office and Windows software, LinkedIn and Xbox.

past.label: Azure revenue, same quarter last year
past.detail: Azure is Microsoft's cloud business, where most AI demand lands.

current.label: Latest quarter revenue (Jul–Sep 2026)
current.detail: Azure $33.2B, up 48%. Microsoft Cloud $63.9B, up 30%. Operating income up 21%.

future.label: Capital spending this quarter
future.detail: Up from $19.4B a year earlier: a large bet on future AI demand.

drivers: Companies moving work to the cloud
AI tools built into Office and Azure
Recurring subscription revenue
risks: Huge data-center spending must pay off
Competition from Amazon and Google
Regulation of AI and big tech
watch: Azure growth rate
Capital spending versus revenue growth
Operating margin
why: Businesses keep moving their computing to the cloud, and AI is speeding that up. Azure grew 48% last quarter, and Microsoft's CFO says customer demand still exceeds the capacity it can supply. Its commercial backlog, contracts signed but not yet delivered, reached $677B, up 73%.

company: December-quarter revenue of $96B to $97.1B, up from $92.3B
Capital spending roughly doubled from a year ago to add data-center capacity
analysts: The key debate: whether the AI spending pays back with enough profit to keep margins high

scenarios.bull: AI services become a large, high-margin business on top of steady software subscriptions.
scenarios.base: Steady high-teens growth, with margins pressured somewhat by data-center costs.
scenarios.bear: AI demand cools after heavy spending, leaving costly unused capacity.

name: Eli Lilly
what: Pharmaceutical company behind Mounjaro and Zepbound, leading diabetes and obesity medicines.
drivers: Demand for obesity and diabetes drugs
New pill versions and new uses for existing drugs
An aging, heavier world population
risks: Drug price pressure from governments
Competition from Novo Nordisk and new entrants
Trial results and safety findings
watch: Mounjaro and Zepbound growth
Pricing deals and policy
Pipeline trial results
why: Mounjaro and Zepbound, Lilly's diabetes and weight-loss medicines, are among the fastest-selling drugs ever. Together they brought in about $16B last quarter. Obesity affects hundreds of millions of people, and these drugs work better than anything before them.

company: 2026 revenue guidance raised to $91–92B, from $85–87B
analysts: In January 2026, Leerink projected $94.3B in revenue by 2027; Lilly's own 2026 guidance is already close to that path
Truist sees combined peak sales of its obesity drugs, including the oral pill orforglipron, reaching $101B a year

scenarios.bull: Oral obesity pills widen the market, Medicare coverage expands, and new drugs like retatrutide add another leg of growth.
scenarios.base: Strong growth continues, with prices gradually falling as competition and government pressure increase.
scenarios.bear: Competitors match its results, prices drop sharply, or trials disappoint.

name: Costco
what: Membership warehouse retailer that earns much of its profit from membership fees.

current.label: Fiscal 2026 net sales (year to Aug 2026)
current.detail: Q4 comparable sales up 9.4%. 84.1 million paid members, 92.3% renewal in the US and Canada.

future.label: Membership fees, latest quarter
future.detail: Up 7.3%. Recurring, high-margin income that funds low prices.

drivers: Very loyal members
Low prices that win share in any economy
New warehouses, including abroad
risks: Stock usually trades at a high valuation
Thin margins on goods
Consumer spending slowdowns
watch: Renewal rate
Comparable sales growth
New warehouse openings
why: Costco earns loyalty through low prices and makes much of its profit from membership fees, which 92% of US and Canadian members renew. Sales grew 10.1% in fiscal 2026, and its 3.0% net margin was the highest in ten years. Higher gas prices added about 3% to sales, a boost that may not last.

company: Plans to open 33 warehouses in fiscal 2027, up from 28 in fiscal 2026
analysts: Consensus expects sales growth of about 7.5% and profit growth of about 9.6% across fiscal 2027–2028
The stock trades at about 45 times last year's earnings, a high price for steady growth

scenarios.bull: International expansion and digital sales speed up growth, and members keep renewing at record rates.
scenarios.base: Steady high-single-digit growth, the reliable compounding it is known for.
scenarios.bear: Growth slows to normal retail levels and its high valuation shrinks.

name: GE Vernova
what: Builds gas turbines, wind turbines and grid equipment that generate and move electricity.

past.label: Orders, latest quarter
past.detail: Up 96% organically: demand is running far ahead of what it can ship.

future.label: Backlog of orders
future.detail: 2026 revenue guidance raised to $46.5–47.5B; free cash flow guidance $16–17B.

drivers: Electricity demand from data centers and factories
Aging grids that need replacing
Long waiting lists for turbines
risks: Wind business has struggled
Project delays and cost overruns
Demand forecasts could prove too high
watch: Orders versus revenue
Backlog growth
Margins on new orders
why: Electricity demand is rising for the first time in decades because of data centers, factories and electrification. Utilities need gas turbines and grid equipment, and GE Vernova has years of orders waiting: orders nearly doubled last quarter and its backlog is $197B.

company: 2026 revenue guidance of $46.5–47.5B, raised in October
2028 targets set in December 2025: about $52B revenue, a 20% adjusted EBITDA margin and about $200B backlog. The backlog is already near that target.
analysts: UBS called the 2028 targets a very strong update when they were raised

scenarios.bull: Power demand keeps rising faster than expected, and long order queues let it raise prices.
scenarios.base: It works through its backlog with steady growth and improving margins.
scenarios.bear: Data-center building slows, orders are delayed or cancelled, and the wind business keeps losing money.

name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC)
what: Manufactures the most advanced chips in the world for other companies, including the AI chips designed by Nvidia and others.

past.label: Net income a year earlier (Jul–Sep 2025)
past.detail: Profit grew 68.7% to NT$763.1B in the latest quarter.

current.label: Latest quarter revenue (Jul–Sep 2026)
current.detail: Up 50.9% in Taiwan dollars. Gross margin 66.4%; 7-nanometer and more advanced chips were 79% of wafer revenue.

future.label: Q4 2026 revenue guidance
future.detail: Company guidance: gross margin 65–67%, operating margin 56.5–58.5%, as its 2-nanometer technology ramps up.

drivers: Demand for AI chips from data centers
The shift to 2- and 3-nanometer manufacturing
Very high margins on leading-edge production
risks: Geopolitical tension around Taiwan
Dependence on a few large customers such as Nvidia
Huge spending needed to stay ahead; currency swings affect reported results
watch: Quarterly revenue versus guidance
Share of revenue from the newest nodes
Gross margin as new factories open
why: Almost every advanced AI chip, whoever designs it, is made in TSMC's factories, so it earns from the AI build-out no matter which chip designer wins. Demand for its newest processes is running ahead of what it can produce, which lets it keep margins near two-thirds of revenue: 7-nanometer and newer technologies were 79% of wafer revenue last quarter.

company: Q4 2026 revenue of US$52.3–54.3B with a 65–67% gross margin (Oct 15, 2026)
Full-year 2026 revenue growth of about 44% in US dollars, raised from slightly above 40% in July
2026 capital spending of US$60–64B, with 2026–2028 spending significantly higher than the previous three years
analysts: Q3 profit came in slightly ahead of analyst estimates compiled by LSEG (Oct 15, 2026)
Futurum Group said the Q4 guidance midpoint was ahead of prior Street expectations (Oct 20, 2026)

scenarios.bull: AI demand keeps outrunning supply, the 2-nanometer ramp goes smoothly and margins stay near record levels.
scenarios.base: Revenue keeps growing with AI spending while heavy factory investment and new overseas plants trim margins slightly.
scenarios.bear: Big customers cut AI chip orders, tension around Taiwan disrupts operations or trade, or new factories cost more than planned.

name: Sony Group
what: Owns PlayStation, one of the world's largest music companies, a Hollywood film and TV studio, and the leading maker of camera image sensors.

past.label: Operating income, Jul–Sep 2025
past.detail: Rose 45% to ¥622.3B in the latest quarter; operating margin went from 13.8% to 18.1%.

current.label: Latest quarter sales (Jul–Sep 2026)
current.detail: Up about 4% at constant exchange rates. Net income rose 44% to ¥449.6B. Pictures sales rose 48% and games operating income 83%.

future.label: FY2026 operating income forecast (year to March 2027)
future.detail: Company forecast raised Nov 5 from ¥1.72T; sales forecast raised to ¥13.0T from ¥12.5T, with a 35-yen dividend, up 10 yen.

drivers: PlayStation games and network services
Film and TV hits in Pictures
Music streaming
A weak yen that lifts overseas earnings in yen
risks: About 6 points of the 10% sales growth came from the weak yen and would reverse if it strengthens
Image sensor sales fell 6% on weaker smartphone demand
Film results depend on hits and swing year to year
Changing US tariff policy on hardware
watch: Game segment profit as the console ages
Image sensor sales to phone makers
Whether the yen stays weak
Results against the raised full-year forecast
why: Sony has turned into an entertainment company that makes money from the content people return to: games, music catalogs, films and shows, sold digitally at high margins. In the July–September quarter games operating income rose 83% and Pictures sales 48%, and the company raised its full-year profit forecast by 9%. A weak yen helps: the dollar averaged 159.3 yen in the quarter versus 147.4 a year earlier, which inflates overseas earnings when counted in yen.

company: FY2026 sales of ¥13.0T, operating income ¥1.87T and net income ¥1.33T, all raised on Nov 5, 2026
Image sensor sales essentially flat for the year at ¥2.12T, with operating income forecast raised to ¥450B
Forecast assumes about 153 yen per dollar for the rest of the year, below the quarter's 159.3 average
analysts: Zacks attributed the quarter's sales growth to gaming and Pictures strength (Nov 5, 2026)

scenarios.bull: Games and music keep growing digital sales at high margins, Pictures has more hits, and sensor demand from phone makers recovers.
scenarios.base: Entertainment keeps growing while sensors stay flat, and the raised forecast is roughly met.
scenarios.bear: The yen strengthens and shrinks overseas earnings, console sales fade, and smartphone sensor demand keeps falling.

sources.name: Sony Group Q2 FY2026 results presentation (SEC Form 6-K), Nov 5, 2026

name: Richemont
what: Owns Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels and Buccellati jewelry and watchmakers including IWC, Jaeger-LeCoultre and Vacheron Constantin.

current.label: Sales, six months to Sep 2026
current.detail: Up 17% at constant exchange rates. Operating profit rose 33% to €3.13B (25.5% margin; 23.6% excluding €229M of one-time tariff-related gains). Jewelry sales rose 19% at constant rates with a 35.3% margin.

future.label: Company outlook
future.detail: The chairman expects the environment to remain volatile for the foreseeable future and says the watch recovery is unlikely to be linear. Net cash stood at €7.73B.

drivers: Jewelry demand at Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels
Sales through its own stores, now 78% of the total
Americas sales up 23% and Japan up 30% at constant rates
Price increases that mostly offset higher gold costs
risks: High gold prices squeeze gross margin; excluding the tariff item, gross margin fell 0.7 points
Growth slowed to 13% in the second quarter from 20% in the first
Middle East and Africa sales fell 2% amid the regional conflict
Watch demand in China remains soft
Currency hedging losses of €418M outweighed €316M of currency gains
watch: Jewelry growth each quarter
Gross margin as gold prices move
Watchmaker margins, 8.8% this half
Spending by Chinese and Middle East shoppers
why: Richemont is a jewelry business more than a watch business, and jewelry is where luxury demand is strongest: its jewelry houses grew sales 19% at constant rates and earned a 35.3% operating margin, against 8.8% at the watchmakers. Selling mostly through its own stores (72% retail, 6% online) gives it control over pricing, which let it raise prices enough to mostly offset the higher cost of gold. Operating cash flow rose 35% to €2.5B.

company: No numeric forecast; management expects a volatile environment for the foreseeable future (Nov 13, 2026)
Watchmaker recovery described as unlikely to be linear, with soft demand in China (Nov 13, 2026)
analysts: Shares opened more than 4% lower on Nov 13, 2026 even though first-half net profit beat forecasts (Yahoo Finance)

scenarios.bull: Jewelry keeps growing in the double digits, price increases keep pace with gold, and watch demand in China recovers.
scenarios.base: Jewelry growth slows toward the second-quarter pace while watches improve gradually and margins hold.
scenarios.bear: Gold keeps rising faster than prices can follow, wealthy shoppers in China and the Gulf pull back, and growth slows further.

sources.name: Richemont, results for the six months ended 30 September 2026, Nov 13, 2026
Yahoo Finance, Stock market today, Nov 13, 2026

name: HDFC Bank
theme: India's credit boom and rising rates
what: An Indian bank lending to households and businesses and owning stakes in HDFC Life, HDFC AMC and HDB Financial Services.

past.label: Consolidated net profit, Jul–Sep 2025
past.detail: Net interest income, the gap between interest earned and paid, was ₹31,552 crore at the bank level.

current.label: Consolidated net profit, Jul–Sep 2026
current.detail: Net interest income rose 9.7% to ₹34,619 crore. Deposits grew 18.8% and gross advances about 16%. Net interest margin slipped to 3.16% of total assets. Gross bad loans fell to 1.11% of loans and net bad loans to 0.37%. Treasury trading gains fell about ₹1,610 crore from a year earlier.

future.label: Company plans
future.detail: Anup Bagchi takes over as managing director and CEO from Sashidhar Jagdishan after the quarter, in late October 2026. The bank gave no loan-growth or margin forecast in the reports read. Capital adequacy is about 18.9%, with a CET1 ratio of 17.1%.

drivers: Deposits growing faster than loans (18.8% vs about 16%)
SME and mid-market lending up 23.5%
Improving asset quality
Profits from insurance, asset management and consumer-finance subsidiaries
risks: Margins at a record low as time deposits (up 22.8%) grow faster than cheap current and savings accounts, now 31.6% of deposits
Rising Indian inflation and RBI rate hikes could lift funding costs and slow borrowers
Profit growth of about 5% trails loan growth
Leadership change at the top
Rupee moves affect returns for holders of the US-listed shares
watch: Net interest margin each quarter
Share of low-cost current and savings deposits
Bad-loan ratios as rates rise
The new CEO's first targets
why: HDFC Bank is growing its balance sheet steadily: deposits rose 18.8% and advances about 16%, while bad loans keep falling, a sign of conservative lending. Its core lending income rose 9.7%, but headline profit grew only about 5%, partly because treasury gains shrank and margins narrowed as it paid more for deposits. Shares were down about 28% in 2026 by mid-October, against an 11.5% fall in the Nifty 50, per Kotak Neo.

company: No numeric guidance in the Q2 FY27 reports read; management commentary was awaited (Oct 2026)
CEO transition to Anup Bagchi after the September quarter (Oct 2026)
analysts: Standalone profit came in slightly below the LSEG consensus of ₹19,526 crore, per NiftyTrader (Oct 17, 2026)
Shares fell about 2% in early trade after the results, to ₹712, per Kotak Neo (Oct 19, 2026)

scenarios.bull: Deposit growth stays strong, cheaper deposits return, margins recover, and the new CEO lifts loan growth without hurting credit quality.
scenarios.base: Loans and deposits keep growing in the mid-teens while margins stay near current levels and profit grows modestly.
scenarios.bear: RBI hikes push funding costs higher, margins keep shrinking, and rising inflation squeezes borrowers so bad loans turn up.

name: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group
theme: Japan's return to positive interest rates
what: Japan's largest banking group, lending, taking deposits and earning fees at home and abroad, and owning a large stake in Morgan Stanley.

past.label: Net income, Apr–Sep 2025
past.detail: Net income attributable to owners was ¥1,292.9 billion; net interest income was ¥1,440.0 billion.

current.label: Net income, Apr–Sep 2026
current.detail: A record first half. Net interest income rose 28.6% to ¥1.85 trillion and net fees and commissions about 14%. Higher Japanese interest rates added about ¥140 billion to net operating profit and the weaker yen about ¥35 billion. Equity-method earnings, helped by Morgan Stanley, rose to ¥473 billion. Return on equity was 14.5%, up from 12.5%.

future.label: Company target, year to March 2027
future.detail: Raised from ¥2.7 trillion on Nov 13, 2026; the first half delivered about 58% of it. Net operating profit target unchanged at ¥2.9 trillion and credit-cost target at ¥350 billion. Dividend forecast raised to ¥100 a share, from ¥86 last year, plus a buyback of up to ¥200 billion in the second half.

drivers: Higher yen interest rates widening lending margins
Loan growth in Japan and overseas
Rising fee income
Earnings from its Morgan Stanley stake
risks: ¥196 billion of losses on debt securities in the half, mostly from selling US mortgage-backed bonds while rebalancing
The company warns it may need significant additional loan-loss provisions tied to the Middle East situation
A slowing Japanese economy could raise bad loans
Profits are flattered by a weak yen and could shrink if it strengthens
Costs are rising, including for inflation and cybersecurity
watch: Bank of Japan rate decisions
Net interest income each quarter
Credit costs against the ¥350 billion target
Bond portfolio gains or losses
Progress on the buyback
why: After decades of near-zero rates, Japan's banks can finally earn a real margin on lending, and MUFG's net interest income jumped 28.6% in the first half. Fees and its Morgan Stanley stake added more, lifting return on equity to 14.5%. Management raised its profit target and dividend and added a buyback, a sign it expects the gains to hold.

company: Full-year net income target raised to ¥2.8 trillion from ¥2.7 trillion (Nov 13, 2026)
Annual dividend forecast ¥100 a share; buyback of up to ¥200 billion in the second half (Nov 13, 2026)
Net operating profit target kept at ¥2.9 trillion 'considering future growth initiatives' (Nov 13, 2026)
analysts: No analyst estimates were given in the sources read; an investor briefing is scheduled for Nov 17, 2026

scenarios.bull: The Bank of Japan keeps raising rates gradually, lending margins widen further, loan losses stay near target and buybacks continue.
scenarios.base: Rates edge up, net interest income keeps growing, and the group lands near its ¥2.8 trillion target with credit costs around plan.
scenarios.bear: Japan's slowdown and the Middle East conflict push loan losses well above target, bond losses recur, and a stronger yen shrinks overseas profits.

sources.name: MUFG Form 6-K (H1 FY2026 results), SEC, Nov 13, 2026

name: Rheinmetall
what: Germany's largest defense company, making ammunition, artillery, armored vehicles, air defense, naval ships and military digital systems.

past.label: Sales, Jan–Sep 2025
past.detail: Nine-month sales were €6,057 million with an operating result of €795 million, a 13.1% margin. Full-year 2025 sales were €9,935 million.

current.label: Sales, Jan–Sep 2026
current.detail: Sales rose 38% to €8,376 million and the operating result rose about 69% to a record €1,339 million, a 16.0% margin. Air defense sales grew 63%, weapons and ammunition 34%, digital systems 29% and vehicles 20%; the naval business was added from February 2026. Earnings per share from continuing operations were €14.44, against €7.83.

future.label: Backlog, Sep 30, 2026
future.detail: Up from €56.7 billion a year earlier, including signed framework agreements; new nominations were €19.1 billion in nine months. Full-year 2026 guidance was cut to sales of around €13.2 billion, from €13.7–14.2 billion, and an operating margin of around 18.5%, from around 19%.

drivers: European governments raising defense budgets
Ammunition and artillery demand
Air defense orders, where backlog rose 81%
Large German vehicle and digital programs
Acquisitions such as the naval business
risks: Revenue depends on government budgets, parliamentary approvals and contract timing
2026 guidance was cut because Germany's Arminius vehicle program and artillery acceptance tests slipped
Operating free cash flow was −€1.7 billion in nine months as inventories and working capital grew
Management told analysts the backlog will fall short of its €100 billion-plus end-2026 aim without Arminius
A ceasefire or peace deal in Ukraine could change how urgently governments buy
watch: Bundestag approval of large German orders
Whether full-year sales reach about €13.2 billion
Operating free cash flow turning positive as guided
Targets at the upcoming Capital Markets Day
Ukraine peace talks and European defense budgets
why: Europe is rebuilding its armed forces, and Rheinmetall makes many of the things being ordered, from shells to air defense. Nine-month sales rose 38% and profit grew faster, lifting the margin to 16%, while the backlog reached €78 billion, more than eight times 2025 sales. The catch is timing: when governments delay approvals or tests, revenue slips, as the guidance cut shows.

company: 2026 sales of around €13.2 billion, cut from €13.7–14.2 billion (Nov 5, 2026)
2026 operating margin of around 18.5%, from around 19% (Nov 5, 2026)
Operating result expected to improve in 2026, including acquisitions (Nov 5, 2026)
Management told analysts it still expects positive operating free cash flow for 2026 and capex above €1 billion (Nov 5, 2026 call)
analysts: No analyst estimates were given in the sources read

scenarios.bull: German parliament approves delayed programs quickly, European budgets keep rising, the backlog converts to sales on time and cash flow turns positive.

scenarios.bear: Approvals and acceptance tests keep slipping, a peace deal in Ukraine cools urgency, and cash stays tied up in inventory.

name: Alibaba Group
what: China's largest e-commerce company, running Taobao and Tmall, which is turning itself into an AI cloud and computing provider.

past.label: Revenue, June quarter 2026
past.detail: Revenue was RMB 268,953 million (US$39.6 billion), up 9%. AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue was RMB 48,437 million, up 45%. Adjusted EBITA fell 30% and net income fell 75% as the company spent heavily on quick commerce and AI; capex rose 75% to RMB 67,678 million.

current.label: Revenue, September quarter 2026
current.detail: Revenue rose 10% to RMB 271.5 billion, slightly ahead of the RMB 269.81 billion analysts expected (LSEG). AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue rose 53% to about RMB 61 billion, with segment adjusted EBITA up 121% to RMB 8.8 billion. Customer management revenue, mainly merchant fees on Taobao and Tmall, fell 5%. Net income tripled to RMB 64.4 billion, helped by investment gains; non-GAAP net income rose 92% to RMB 19.9 billion, but adjusted earnings per ADS of RMB 8.10 missed the RMB 11.16 expected. Free cash flow was an outflow of RMB 34.47 billion and capex rose 60% to RMB 50.48 billion.

future.label: Data-centre plan
future.detail: In September Alibaba announced plans to expand global data-centre capacity to more than 20 gigawatts by 2032. It raised about $10 billion through a share placement in August to fund AI infrastructure, its T-Head chip unit has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong listing, and a new AI processor is due for commercial release in early 2027. The CFO said it aims to return to positive free cash flow.

drivers: AI cloud demand, with external recurring cloud revenue up 67%
AI-related product revenue growing at triple digits for 13 straight quarters
Narrowing losses in Taobao Instant Commerce
In-house AI chips
risks: Heavy capex has pushed free cash flow negative
Core merchant fee revenue fell 5%
Profit was flattered by investment gains; adjusted EPS missed forecasts
US export controls and China–US tensions affect access to advanced chips
AI Labs and Applications losses tripled to RMB 10.5 billion
Shares down about 40% this year, per Reuters
watch: Cloud growth staying above 50%
Whether free cash flow turns positive as targeted
Customer management revenue trend on Taobao and Tmall
Quick-commerce losses
T-Head listing and chip launch in early 2027
why: Alibaba is spending heavily to become China's main AI cloud provider, and that part of the business is growing fast: cloud revenue rose 53% and its profit more than doubled. The older shopping business is under pressure, with merchant fees down 5%, and the build-out is consuming cash, so the company is betting today's spending turns into tomorrow's cloud profits.

company: Plans more than 20 GW of global data-centre capacity by 2032 (announced Sep 2026)
Disciplined AI investment focused on return on capital, targeting positive free cash flow (CFO, Nov 19, 2026)
New AI processor commercial release in early 2027 (Nov 2026)
analysts: Analysts expected September-quarter revenue of RMB 269.81 billion and adjusted EPADS of RMB 11.16 (LSEG via Reuters, Nov 19, 2026)

scenarios.bull: Cloud demand keeps growing above 50%, new chips ease supply limits, quick-commerce losses keep shrinking and free cash flow turns positive.
scenarios.base: Cloud grows strongly while the shopping business stays flat to down and heavy capex keeps cash flow weak for a while.
scenarios.bear: Chip restrictions or price wars slow cloud growth, merchant revenue keeps falling, and spending fails to earn its cost of capital.

sources.name: Alibaba June quarter 2026 results (SEC Form 6-K exhibit), Aug 20, 2026

name: Nu Holdings (Nubank)
what: A branchless digital bank serving about 143 million customers in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia through credit cards, loans and savings accounts in an app.

past.label: Revenue, Q3 2025
past.detail: Revenue was $4,317.2 million and net income $782.7 million in the third quarter of 2025, with 127.0 million customers, a $30.4 billion credit portfolio, $38.8 billion of deposits, a 20.3% efficiency ratio and 31% return on equity.

current.label: Revenue, Q3 2026
current.detail: Revenue rose to $6,258.5 million, up 37% at constant currency (about 45% in reported dollars). Net income was a record $1,091.6 million, up 31% at constant currency, with 32% return on equity. Customers reached 142.6 million, with Mexico at 16.6 million (+27%) and Colombia at 6.1 million (+62%). The credit portfolio grew 33% to $41.6 billion and deposits 19% to $47.5 billion. The efficiency ratio improved to 19.3%. Loans 90+ days overdue rose to 7.3% from 6.7% a year earlier, with coverage of 234%.

future.label: 2026 efficiency ratio guidance
future.detail: Nu lowered its full-year 2026 efficiency ratio guidance to 19%–19.5% from around 20%, and expects it to rise in the fourth quarter. It launched Nu US on Sep 10, 2026, offering accounts through partner Lead Bank, and Nu Global on Oct 15, 2026 with customers in 37 countries, and has committed that these expansions will add up to 100 basis points to its efficiency ratio in each of 2026 and 2027. Mexico's third quarter was its first operating as a bank.

drivers: Fast customer growth in Mexico and Colombia
Rising revenue per active customer, $17.7 a month vs $13.8 a year earlier
Cheap deposits, costing 87% of Brazil's interbank rate
Very low costs per customer from having no branches
Record personal-loan originations in Brazil
risks: Overdue loans are rising: 90+ day NPLs 7.3% vs 6.7% a year earlier
Heavy reliance on Brazil, where management assumes economic conditions worsen
Lending is mostly unsecured credit cards and personal loans, which suffer first in downturns
Currency swings: results in dollars move with the Brazilian real and Mexican peso
New US and global ventures add costs before they earn revenue
Interest-rate caps and other regulation in its markets
watch: NPL ratios and credit-loss provisions each quarter
Mexico growth now that it operates as a bank
Efficiency ratio against the 19%–19.5% guidance
Early traction of Nu US and Nu Global
Investor Day on Dec 8, 2026
why: Nu grows fast because it reaches people who were poorly served by traditional banks, at a fraction of their cost: its efficiency ratio of about 19% means it spends roughly 19 cents to earn each dollar of income. Cheap deposits and higher revenue per customer have pushed quarterly profit above $1 billion. The price of that growth is credit risk, and overdue loans are edging up.

company: Full-year 2026 efficiency ratio of 19%–19.5%, rising in Q4 (Q3 2026 release, Nov 12, 2026)
Nu US and Nu Global to weigh on efficiency by up to 100 bps in each of 2026 and 2027 (Nov 12, 2026)
Effective tax rate expected in the low-to-mid 20s% in 2027 (earnings call, Nov 12, 2026, per Investing.com)
analysts: Q3 accounting revenue of $5.82 billion and EPS of $0.22 came in below consensus of $5.91 billion and $0.23 (Investing.com, Nov 2026)

scenarios.bull: Mexico and Colombia keep adding millions of customers, revenue per customer keeps rising, overdue loans stabilise and the US and global launches gain traction without eroding efficiency.
scenarios.base: Growth slows from very high levels as Brazil matures, credit quality drifts modestly worse, and profits keep rising with Mexico as the main new engine.
scenarios.bear: A Brazilian downturn or rate shock lifts defaults on unsecured loans, provisions eat into profit, and expansion costs rise faster than new revenue.

name: Walmart
theme: Retail with advertising and membership income
what: The world's largest retailer, selling groceries and general merchandise through stores, Sam's Club warehouses and e-commerce in the US and abroad.

past.label: Total revenue, Q3 FY26
past.detail: Total revenue was $179,496 million in the quarter to October 2025. For the full fiscal year to January 2026, net sales were $706.4 billion, adjusted operating income $31.0 billion and adjusted EPS $2.64.

current.label: Total revenue, Q3 FY27
current.detail: Revenue rose 5.2% (4.5% at constant currency) in the quarter to October 31, 2026. Walmart U.S. comparable sales rose 2.9% excluding fuel, with transactions up 1.5% and average ticket up 1.4%; US e-commerce grew 23% and global e-commerce 17%. Global advertising grew 25% and membership fee revenue 17%. Operating income rose 16.0% to $7.77 billion (adjusted, constant currency: +5.5%) and the gross profit rate rose 28 basis points. Adjusted EPS was $0.65 vs $0.62; GAAP EPS was $0.62 vs $0.77. Year to date, operating cash flow was $29.4 billion, capital spending $22.6 billion and free cash flow $6.8 billion, down $2.0 billion.

future.label: FY27 adjusted EPS guidance
future.detail: On Nov 19, 2026 Walmart raised its fiscal 2027 outlook for the third time: net sales growth of 4.9% to 5.2% at constant currency (from 4.0% to 5.0%), adjusted operating income growth of 8.0% to 8.6% (from 7.0% to 8.5%), and adjusted EPS of $2.84 to $2.89 (from $2.80 to $2.87; originally $2.75 to $2.85). Capital spending is planned at about 4.0% of net sales.

drivers: E-commerce growth, 23% in the US, with stores used as fulfillment hubs
High-margin advertising: Walmart Connect up 36% excluding acquisitions
Membership income from Walmart+ and Sam's Club, fees up 17%
More customer visits: US transactions up 1.5%, Sam's Club up 5.1%
Growth in China, with net sales up 28.5% at constant currency
risks: Heavy capital spending is cutting free cash flow, down $2.0 billion year to date
Over $2 billion of extra costs this year from fuel, transportation and investments
Tariffs and trade restrictions named as risks in its forward-looking statements
Drug price regulation: about 70 bps drag on US comps from pharmacy deflation
Sam's Club operating income fell 15.8% as a new membership bundle dilutes profit
Inventory up 8.1%, faster than sales
watch: Walmart U.S. comps and the transaction vs ticket split
Advertising and membership growth as a share of profit
Free cash flow against capital spending
Sam's Club profit as the membership bundle is lapped
Fourth-quarter holiday results against the raised outlook
why: Walmart is growing faster than its size would suggest because it is turning its stores and traffic into newer, higher-margin businesses: online delivery, advertising sold to brands, and paid memberships. More customers are visiting, which matters more than price-driven ticket growth. On a day the S&P 500 fell 3.70%, its shares rose about 1.5%, showing how investors treat steady essentials as shelter in a sell-off.

company: FY27 net sales growth of 4.9%–5.2% at constant currency (Q3 FY27 release, Nov 19, 2026)
FY27 adjusted operating income growth of 8.0%–8.6% cc and adjusted EPS of $2.84–$2.89 (Nov 19, 2026)
Capital spending of about 4.0% of net sales (Nov 19, 2026)
analysts: Revenue of $188.8 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.65 beat Wall Street expectations, EPS by $0.01 (Investing.com, Nov 19, 2026)

scenarios.bull: E-commerce turns more profitable as volumes grow, advertising and membership keep rising faster than sales, and heavy investment starts lifting free cash flow.
scenarios.base: Sales grow mid-single digits, profit grows faster on advertising and membership, and free cash flow stays squeezed by capital spending.
scenarios.bear: Tariffs, fuel and wage costs outrun price increases, shoppers trade down, and spending on automation and delivery fails to pay back.

name: Nova
theme: Measurement tools for advanced chips and AI memory
what: Nova makes metrology systems that measure materials, dimensions and chemistry on silicon wafers during production, so chipmakers can control their manufacturing processes.

past.label: Revenue, Q3 2025
past.detail: Revenue was $224.6 million in the quarter to September 2025, with GAAP net income of $61.4 million, or $1.90 per diluted share, and a GAAP operating margin of 28%.

current.label: Revenue, Q3 2026
current.detail: Record revenue of $287.8 million, up 28% from a year earlier and 13% from the prior quarter. Products were $231.9 million and services $56.0 million. GAAP gross margin was 58% and GAAP operating margin rose to 32% (non-GAAP 36%). GAAP net income was $90.0 million, or $2.64 per diluted share (non-GAAP $2.86). Operating cash flow was $138.1 million and the company bought back $38.5 million of shares. Records came in advanced packaging, driven by HBM memory and advanced logic, and in memory metrology.

future.label: Q4 2026 revenue guidance
future.detail: For the quarter ending December 31, 2026, Nova guided to revenue of $305 million to $315 million, GAAP diluted EPS of $2.78 to $2.93 and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $3.03 to $3.18 (Nov 5, 2026).

drivers: Record advanced packaging revenue from HBM and advanced logic capacity expansions
Record memory revenue in dimensional and materials metrology
Smaller, more complex chips need more measurement steps
Recurring service revenue of $56 million a quarter
Rising margins: GAAP operating margin up from 28% to 32% in a year
risks: Dependence on a small number of large chipmaker customers
Semiconductor demand is cyclical; chip stocks fell 10.7% on Nov 20, 2026
Export restrictions and risks of doing business with China
A single manufacturing facility per product line
Exposure to conflict in Israel, where it is based
About $735 million of convertible notes outstanding
watch: Q4 revenue against the $305–$315 million guide
Advanced packaging and memory as a share of sales
China revenue as export rules change
Margins as revenue grows
Whether AI memory spending holds up after the sell-off
why: Nova sells measuring tools that chipmakers need more of as chips become smaller and are stacked into packages such as the high-bandwidth memory used in AI systems. Its revenue grew 28% in a year and profits grew faster, because extra sales on a mostly fixed cost base widen margins. Its fortunes depend on how much a few large chipmakers spend, which ties it to the AI investment cycle.

company: Q4 2026 revenue of $305–$315 million (Q3 release, Nov 5, 2026)
Q4 2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $2.78–$2.93 and non-GAAP $3.03–$3.18 (Nov 5, 2026)
analysts: No analyst estimates were given in the sources read

scenarios.bull: Chipmakers keep adding HBM and advanced logic capacity, Nova's packaging and memory records continue, and margins keep widening as revenue grows.
scenarios.base: Revenue lands within guidance and growth continues at a slower pace as the AI build-out matures, with margins holding near current levels.
scenarios.bear: The AI sell-off turns into spending cuts at a few big customers, export rules squeeze China sales, or conflict disrupts operations, and revenue and margins fall back.

name: Coupang
theme: Same-day delivery and the cost of rebuilding trust
what: Coupang runs South Korea's largest online store with its own warehouses and drivers, plus food delivery, video streaming and a growing business in Taiwan, all bundled into a paid WOW membership.

past.label: Revenue, Q3 2025
past.detail: In the quarter to September 2025, net revenue was $9.267 billion, with operating income of $162 million, net income of $95 million and adjusted EBITDA of $413 million (4.5% margin). Product Commerce had 24.7 million active customers, up 10%, and free cash flow was $442 million in the quarter and $1.3 billion over twelve months.

current.label: Revenue, Q3 2026
current.detail: Net revenue was $9.962 billion, up 7.5% (11% in constant currency, after 10% in Q2 and 8% in Q1). Developing offerings, including Taiwan, grew 27% in constant currency to $1.588 billion. Active customers rose only 2% to 25.2 million after a personal-data leak drove some away. A July fire at a fulfillment center in Incheon cost $248 million, leaving a GAAP operating loss of $450 million and a net loss of $501 million. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $116 million (1.2% margin), and free cash flow was negative $409 million over twelve months.

future.label: Q4 2026 revenue growth guidance
future.detail: Management guided to constant-currency revenue growth of 13% to 14% in Q4 2026 and an adjusted EBITDA margin 50 to 150 basis points above Q3's 1.2%. It called Q3 the low point for Product Commerce margins, expects them to return near pre-incident levels by mid-2027, and raised the top of its loss guidance for developing offerings to fund Taiwan (reported Nov 3–4, 2026).

drivers: Constant-currency growth re-accelerated from 8% to 11% over three quarters
Taiwan WOW membership more than doubled from a year earlier
Dawn delivery now reaches more than half of Taiwan's population
Korean WOW membership at a record
Developing offerings growing 27% in constant currency
risks: Customers lost after the data leak have not fully returned, and winning them back costs money
Korean fines: $410 million set aside in Q2 2026 for sanctions linked to the data leak, plus later fines reported over food delivery and competition rules
Margins near their lowest: adjusted EBITDA margin 1.2% against 4.5% a year earlier
Negative twelve-month free cash flow and cash down from $6.32 billion to $5.44 billion in 2026
Taiwan expansion widens losses before it pays off
Fixed warehouse costs while volumes recover slowly after the fire
watch: Whether active customers start growing again
Product Commerce margin recovery toward mid-2027
Q4 constant-currency growth against the 13–14% guide
Free cash flow turning positive again
Further Korean regulatory fines
why: Coupang built a delivery network in Korea that rivals find hard to copy, and sales are still growing at a double-digit pace in local currency. But 2026 shows how a data leak, a warehouse fire and regulatory fines can wipe out thin retail margins: it swung from a $95 million profit to a $501 million loss in a year. It matters now as a test of whether a scale advantage survives a loss of customer trust.

company: Q4 2026 constant-currency revenue growth of 13–14% (Nov 3, 2026)
Adjusted EBITDA margin up 50–150 basis points from Q3 in Q4 2026 (Nov 3, 2026)
Product Commerce margins near pre-incident levels by mid-2027 (Nov 4, 2026)
analysts: Consensus Q3 revenue was about $9.74–$9.75 billion, which Coupang beat by about 2% (Earnings Whispers; S&P via StockStory, Nov 3, 2026)
Consensus Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $192.1 million, which Coupang missed at $116 million (StockStory, Nov 3, 2026)
Analysts expect about 12.9% revenue growth over the next 12 months (S&P via StockStory, Nov 3, 2026)

scenarios.bull: Customers return, warehouse volumes recover, margins rebuild toward pre-incident levels by mid-2027, and Taiwan grows into a second profitable market.
scenarios.base: Sales keep growing at a low double-digit pace in local currency while margins recover slowly and fines and Taiwan spending keep profits thin.
scenarios.bear: Trust does not recover, new fines or rules raise costs in Korea, and Taiwan losses keep cash flow negative.
